brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Hex bases piece:0,0,0 and piece:-1,0,0 (half-e) on level 0; piece:0,0,1, piece:0,-1,1 and piece:1,0,1 on level 1. Nothing above level 1.
Footprint is about 416 x 160 x 467 mm. The configurator does not model the bench, so placement on it is not verified.
Two notch drawer frames: notch:0#0,-1#notch4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf, level 0) and notch:1#1,-1#notch3 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm, level 1).

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex-base tower (levels 0 and 1) with two notch drawer frames, one on each storey. Check_build reports meshClash clear with no errors; one info-level open cap face remains. Structure is closed with solid caps and joint bolts. Nothing was dressed with props, and no bins were added inside the cells. Not verified: how the tower sits on a workbench (the configurator does not model that), and material strength or load ratings, which the configurator does not check.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
